A stone is projected horizontally at time t = 0 and falls. Air resistance is negligible. The stone has
a horizontal component of velocity vH and a vertical component of velocity vV.
Which graph shows how vH and vV vary with time t ?

hints: Notice the start values at $t=0$: the projection is horizontal, so $v_H$ starts at the launch speed while $v_V$ starts at $0$.
Connect each direction to forces with air resistance negligible: no horizontal force means zero horizontal acceleration, while weight gives constant vertical acceleration $g$.
Recall what constant velocity and constant acceleration look like on a velocity-time graph: a horizontal line and a straight sloping line from the origin.
walkthrough: At $t=0$ the stone is projected horizontally, so the horizontal component $v_H$ has its full initial value and the vertical component $v_V = 0$.

Horizontally there is no force when air resistance is negligible, so horizontal acceleration is zero and $v_H$ stays constant. On a velocity-time graph this is a horizontal line with a positive intercept.
Vertically the only force is weight, so vertical acceleration is constant at $g$ downward. Hence $v_V = u_V + gt = gt$.
On a velocity-time graph $v_V = gt$ is a straight line through the origin with gradient $g$, showing speed increasing steadily as it falls.
Only the graph with a flat non-zero $v_H$ line and a straight $v_V$ line rising from $0$ matches both components. This is option A.

A.explanation: $v_H$ is constant and non-zero from $t=0$, and $v_V$ starts at zero and increases linearly with gradient $g$.

B.explanation: The labels are swapped - the constant line must be $v_H$ and the line rising from zero must be $v_V$.

C.explanation: $v_V$ cannot curve upward because vertical acceleration is constant, so $v_V = gt$ is a straight line.

D.explanation: $v_V$ must increase from zero as the stone falls, not decrease to zero.
